title: Health & Safety Law: Who Must Do What
whatItIs: The Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 covers all work. It puts duties on employers, the self-employed and employees. HSE inspectors enforce it.

keyFacts.text: Employers MUST ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, the health, safety and welfare at work of all employees.
Employers MUST give the information, instruction, training and supervision needed to keep employees safe.
Employees MUST take reasonable care of themselves and of others affected by what they do, or fail to do.
Employees MUST co-operate with their employer so that it can carry out its health and safety duties.
You MUST NOT intentionally or recklessly interfere with or misuse anything provided for health, safety or welfare.
An employer MUST NOT charge employees for anything it provides to meet a specific legal requirement.

visual.caption: Who has which duty under the 1974 Act

items.title: Employer to employees
items.text: Health, safety and welfare of all employees, so far as is reasonably practicable (s. 2).

items.title: Employer to other people
items.text: Run the work so people it doesn't employ, like the public, aren't put at risk (s. 3).

items.title: Safety policy
items.text: A written health and safety policy, brought to the notice of all employees (s. 2(3)).

items.title: Employees
items.text: Take reasonable care of yourself and others, and co-operate with your employer (s. 7).

items.title: Everyone
items.text: Never interfere with or misuse anything provided for health, safety or welfare (s. 8).

items.title: HSE inspectors
items.text: Can enter sites, talk to workers, take photos and samples, and serve notices.

a.label: Improvement notice
points: Says what is wrong, what to do and by when
Action is suspended while an appeal is heard

b.label: Prohibition notice
points: Stops a process or the use of dangerous equipment
Used where there is a risk of serious personal injury

onTheTest.question: Under the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, which of these is a legal duty of every employee?
options: Take reasonable care of themselves and others
Write the company's health and safety policy
onTheTest.why: Section 7 says every employee must take reasonable care for the health and safety of themselves and others affected by their acts or omissions, and co-operate with their employer.

onTheTest.question: A worker takes down a guard rail to make a job quicker and walks away. Which legal duty has he broken?
options: The duty to write a method statement
The duty not to interfere with things provided for safety
The duty to report injuries to HSE
The duty to provide welfare facilities
onTheTest.why: Section 8: no person shall intentionally or recklessly interfere with or misuse anything provided in the interests of health, safety or welfare.

traps: Safety isn't only the employer's job: employees have legal duties too.
Your employer can't charge you for things the law requires it to provide.
Paying your own tax doesn't automatically make you self-employed under health and safety law.
A prohibition notice still applies during an appeal; an improvement notice is suspended.
